# Nan Blythe

## Overview

- **Age:** 10  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER III. THE INGLESIDE CHILDREN P15](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0015)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER III. THE INGLESIDE CHILDREN P15](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0015)</sub>

- **Status:** alive  _(assumed)_
- **Family:** [Di](../character/di.md) (sibling)

## Appearance

Nan Blythe is described as very pretty, possessing a faultless complexion that brings her mother much satisfaction. She features silky, nut-brown hair complemented by velvety, nut-brown eyes.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER III. THE INGLESIDE CHILDREN P15](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0015)_

## Personality

Nan Blythe is a proud individual who is prone to holding grudges, particularly when it comes to insults directed at her mother. She is motivated by a desire to travel to [Europe](../codex/places.md#europe) alongside [Di](../character/di.md).

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY VANCE P116](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0116), [v5 CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE P30](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0030), [v5 CHAPTER XXIX. A WEIRD TALE P1](../source/v05-c29.md#nw-v05-c29-p0001)_

## History

Nan Blythe enjoyed spending time with her siblings in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley), where they formed a strong friendship with the Meredith children over a shared meal of freshly caught trout. She spent many days playing and sharing stories in the valley alongside her siblings, the [Merediths](../codex/factions.md#merediths), and [Mary Vance](../character/mary-vance.md). When Mary Vance's former guardian passed away, Nan was the one who brought the shocking news to Mary and the gathered children in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley). She also fiercely defended her friend [Faith Meredith](../character/faith.md) alongside her sister [Di](../character/di.md) when [Mary Vance](../character/mary-vance.md) criticized [Faith](../character/faith.md) over a church scandal. As time passed, Nan continued to gather with her family and friends in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley), joining them to read poems, talk about future dreams, and eventually celebrate her brother Jem's final evening before he left for Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy).

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER III. THE INGLESIDE CHILDREN P1](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0001), [v5 CHAPTER III. THE INGLESIDE CHILDREN P5](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0005), [v5 CHAPTER III. THE INGLESIDE CHILDREN P6](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0006), [v5 CHAPTER III. THE INGLESIDE CHILDREN P9](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0009), [v5 CHAPTER III. THE INGLESIDE CHILDREN P16](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0016), [v5 CHAPTER III. THE INGLESIDE CHILDREN P18](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0018), +294 more_

## Quotes

> "Oh, Mary, I’ve news for you. Mrs. Elliott has been over-harbour and what do you think she found out? Mrs. Wiley is dead—she was found dead in bed the morning after you ran away. So you’ll never have to go back to her."
>
> — Nan Blythe — [v5 CHAPTER VIII. MISS CORNELIA INTERVENES P39](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0039)

> "Mother can’t live without trees and I can’t, so what would be the use of going to heaven if there weren’t any trees?"
>
> — Nan Blythe — [v5 CHAPTER XI. A DREADFUL DISCOVERY P34](../source/v05-c11.md#nw-v05-c11-p0034)

> “Won’t you soon have those fish ready, Jem?” said Nan, sniffing with her dainty nose. “The smell makes me awfully hungry.”
>
> — Nan Blythe — [v5 CHAPTER III. THE INGLESIDE CHILDREN P18](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0018)

> "She always used to give me candies when she came to church. But Di is afraid of her."
>
> — Nan Blythe — [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P53](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0053)

> "No—not exactly—but I think it means that heaven will be just like what you’d like it to be."
>
> — Nan Blythe — [v5 CHAPTER XI. A DREADFUL DISCOVERY P42](../source/v05-c11.md#nw-v05-c11-p0042)

## Relationships

### [Carl](../character/carl.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/carl--nan-blythe.md)

Nan and [Carl](../character/carl.md) became close friends after the Meredith and [Blythe](../character/blythe.md) children met in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley) and shared a trout dinner. They regularly gather in the valley alongside their siblings to share stories, hear news, and spend time together as sworn allies.

- Friend of — sworn friends and allies  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P45](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0045)</sub>

### [Di](../character/di.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/di--nan-blythe.md)

[Di](../character/di.md) is Nan's twin sister and constant companion. The two sisters spend much of their time together playing in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley) with their family and the Meredith children, frequently pairing up during social gatherings and jointly coming to the defense of their friends.

### [Mary Vance](../character/mary-vance.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/mary-vance--nan-blythe.md)

Nan interacts with [Mary Vance](../character/mary-vance.md) during play gatherings in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley), though their relationship contains friction. While Nan participates in group activities with Mary, she does not hesitate to push back and defend her friends when Mary criticizes them or frightens the group with dramatic stories.

- Friend of — spending the afternoon together as a treat  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER XVIII. MARY BRINGS EVIL TIDINGS P0](../source/v05-c18.md#nw-v05-c18-p0000)</sub>

### [Una Meredith](../character/una-meredith.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/nan-blythe--una-meredith.md)

Nan and [Una](../character/una-meredith.md) are good friends who belong to the core group of children that routinely meets in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley). They spend their time listening to stories, sharing local news, and supporting one another through various neighborhood occurrences.

- Friend of — defended her against Mary Vance's accusations  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P45](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0045), [v5 CHAPTER XI. A DREADFUL DISCOVERY P14](../source/v05-c11.md#nw-v05-c11-p0014)</sub>
